title: rest: GET /data/:object/:id answers a malformed query (unknown or blank select) as 404, where the dispatcher answers 400
body:
Filing gate: ① a defect with a named landing. Found while landing #26644 (PR #26811, os-dev-report `6448504462` `out_of_scope_findings` class a; contract review `6448772826` item 5). Filed by the `domain:server` seat 1 (`session_01R1q2xdtYgU6FKrZ7LgjPCC`). ⛔ Not a claim. Dedupe: objectstack issues, all states, for "REST GET by id rewrites 400 to 404" and "crud-routes by-id 404 bad input": nearest #25486 and #24768 (closed, different doors), no match.

**What happens.** RestServer's `GET /api/v1/data/:object/:id` catch answers every mapped 400 as 404: `res.status(mapped.status === 400 ? 404 : mapped.status)` at `packages/rest/src/crud-routes.ts:229` on `main`. So a malformed query on an existing record (`?select=nope` today answers `404 INVALID_FIELD`; after #26811 a blank `?select=` answers `404 VALIDATION_ERROR`) is reported as "not found", while the dispatcher's twin route answers the same request 400.

**Why it matters.** A client (or an AI agent) told 404 concludes the record does not exist and stops, when the fault is its own query string. The two hosts disagree on one input, which is the transport-split class this lane keeps closing.

**Wanted.** The by-id catch keeps 404 for a genuinely missing record and answers a request-shape refusal at its own status (400), matching the dispatcher. Pin it with `?select=nope` and a blank `?select=` on an existing record, both hosts, plus the missing-record 404 control. Re-check on current `main` whether other by-id routes in `crud-routes.ts` share the rewrite.

**Clause-②:** the dev measures it (likely `no`: a 404 becomes a 400 for a request that was already refused). **Metadata-protocol:** none expected.
